the_answer: The mixture supports ~53.8B total tokens at four epochs, and the ceiling is ONE source: stack-edu-python, 1.211B unique and out of documents. Corpus as built = 17.15B unique (which is exactly where the released 59.9B run's ~3.5 epochs came from); reachable across untouched files = 6,582B. Only three sources ever bind: everyday-conversations at 0.08B (remove it, as the plan already directs), stack-edu-python at 53.8B, finewiki-en at 902B. Everything else has slack past 1T. At 1T the shortfall is 27.03B unique, of which 21.29B is code, 5.00B is dialogue and 0.74B is wiki.
why_the_aggregate_lies: At 1T the corpus-level ratio is 0.2 epochs while three sources are over the cap. A mixture cannot spend dclm-baseline's 3,746B of headroom on stack-edu-python's shortfall, so `corpus_epochs` is reported only beside `binding_source`. Anyone quoting the aggregate alone will conclude the corpus is fine when it is not.
supply_traps_now_pinned_by_tests: Two, both silent, both pointing the wrong way. (1) A shard manifest's `total_tokens` describes the FETCHED SUBSET while `subset_of.total_tokens` describes the whole released build -- 479M against 5.19B for fineweb-edu, a 10.8x understatement that invents a shortfall. (2) A manifest with no stream position must never reach the density arithmetic: `assess` places an unknown position at file 0 and divides the whole build's tokens by that one file's bytes, reading stack-edu-python's 1.2B as ~13B. Both have regression tests with the real numbers.
the_conservatism_happened_to_be_exact: stack-edu-python and everyday-conversations record no stream position, so they are credited with what they produced and nothing more. For stack-edu-python that is not merely safe, it is right: the Hub resolves its config to 10 files and the original build's recorded position was file 10. Its 2026-08-10 shortfall of 139M is permanent.
cross_checks_on_the_extrapolation: fineweb-edu measures 1,424B reachable against a published ~1.3T for that dataset; dclm-baseline 3,746B against a published multi-trillion corpus. The density extrapolation lands in the right place at both ends, which is worth knowing before anyone plans a successor on these numbers.
this_number_will_go_DOWN: Supply is counted after the released build's dedup and decontamination, which were memory-bounded and reset every 2M kept docs -- exact duplicates outside a reset window survived. Phase 7's own mandate is persistent exact hashes and shared near-duplicate groups across overlapping web sources, which by construction keeps FEWER tokens. Re-measure after the rebuild; do not carry these forward as if the rebuild were free.
